method: Fresh full-glyph/word/numbered-context inspection and original embedded PDF pixel replay, using same-font literal pointed/plain/competing controls and integer nearest-neighbor views only. Three-step rounded lobes with waists classify qubbuts; the mem interior node is compared with a genuinely detached same-page positive and an empty ordinary cavity. A narrow bridge is neither automatic acceptance nor automatic rejection: complete surviving contour must distinguish the competing class. Existing canonical marks identify comparison words but never supply the missing point. No OCR, grammar, expected spelling, translation, image enhancement or new-witness claim.

The exact same-font kaf qubbuts in WIS6:7 repeats the three-step chain; same-font kaf qamats instead has a broad shoulder and one lower central button. Detached alef qubbuts fixes the three-node class independently of the joined kaf control. Existing dagesh and all other scalar positions are preserved.

Below the ordinary alef lower-left foot is a chain of three rounded stamps descending rightward with two narrow waists. It repeats the literal same-font alef qubbuts in WIS13:10. Same-page SUS43 alef qamats has a broad horizontal shoulder and single thin central stem/lower button, unlike the three sidewise lobes of the target. No expected Hebrew reading supplies the point.

A compact rounded node lies inside the completed mem cavity, matching the size and central position of the genuinely detached samepage63 המה mem dagesh. It is connected to the head and lower body by two much thinner vertical necks; the ordinary outer letter contour is separately complete. The samepage63 נמצא plain mem lacks this interior node. The matching added node, rather than bridge connectivity or an absence claim, certifies dagesh. Preserve the existing mem qamats before the new U05BC and all other marks.
